top_signals.title: Super El Niño Could Ease Asia’s LNG Supply Concerns
top_signals.summary: The super El Niño is expected to raise the winter temperatures in South Korea, Japan, and parts of China, potentially easing the gas supply needs in these key Asian LNG importers and leaving more cargoes for Europe, which struggles to fill its gas storage sites to adequate levels for this time of year.  The record El Niño weather pattern in the Pacific is expected to bring warmer winter weather in Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, and parts of China, Bloomberg reports, citing major weather models for the coming winter. …

top_signals.title: How Taiwan Activates Beijing’s Chosen Fear
top_signals.summary:
The standard explanations for why Taiwan is so important to the Chinese Communist Party are familiar: territorial integrity, credibility of deterrence commitments, great power competition with the United States, the strategic value of the first island chain, and the semiconductor industry concentrated in TSMC’s fabrication facilities. These explanations work, but they don’t tell the whole story. top_signals.title: Brazil Election: Lula Narrows Gap to Bolsonaro in PoderData Poll
top_signals.summary: A PoderData/Aya poll showed incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva with 49% of valid votes, compared with 51% for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a statistical tie within the poll’s 1.8 percentage-point margin of error. The presidential runoff will be held on Oct. 25.

top_signals.title: Seema Shah Sees Opportunity in Bank Stocks
top_signals.summary: Seema Shah of Principal Asset Management sees opportunity in bank stocks despite recent weakness. She says earnings, consumer health and the yield curve will be key, with a steeper curve potentially creating a more attractive entry point. She spoke on Bloomberg Brief.  (Source: Bloomberg)
